summary_paraphrase: An unseen voice keeps calling a ginger cat back as it hides, climbs, slips outdoors, unravels a sock, finds a snail and runs into a hen; it comes home and is told to nap in its basket, but in the end it is found asleep on the bed instead.

beats.function: come-back cycle: higher, outside, taking, finding, meeting the hen

characters.name: the cat
characters.change: none: it does what it wants from start to end, including where it sleeps
characters.humor_source: ignores every instruction; the picture shows it doing so

characters.name: the voice
characters.relation_to_protagonist: owner, never shown; every line is spoken to the cat
characters.desire: for the cat to play and then to stay
characters.humor_source: keeps giving orders the cat ignores

characters.name: the hen
characters.relation_to_protagonist: the creature that is not its friend

humor_notes: Humor comes from the gap between the voice's instructions and what the picture shows the cat doing; the last spread is a visual punchline.

repetition.description: the call for the cat to come back opens six spreads, each followed by a new short reason
repetition.why: a listener can join the call, and each turn reveals where the cat has gone

repetition.description: the basket instruction of page 2 returns on page 10 as nap time
repetition.why: frames the outing as away and home again

repetition.description: the call to come back is inverted into a greeting when the cat returns
repetition.why: the change in the familiar line marks the pattern's end

repetition.description: thread, the snail and feathers collect on the cat from page 6 to the last spread, only in the pictures
repetition.why: the cat's body becomes a record of its outing

notes: The text is almost only instructions from an unseen voice; what the cat actually does is carried by the pictures on every spread.
Two of twelve spreads are wordless (5 and 12); the ending twist exists only in the picture.
Objects the text points at without naming (what is not yours, what you have got, who is not your friend) are shown only in the pictures.
The cat carries a growing collection of thread, a snail and feathers: a visual memory of the outing.

strengths: a joinable refrain with a new picture answer each time
the pattern breaks twice: the greeting when the cat returns, then the empty basket
a wordless visual punchline ending that rewards looking
weaknesses: read aloud without pictures the story is mostly lost: 5 of 12 spreads depend on the picture to be understood
the unseen voice is not a character a child can see or identify with

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Mild animal mischief; the hen meeting is comic, not violent. Ends on a nap.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
